jurisdiction.name: Belarus
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Belarus has no AI-specific law or strategy yet. AI is steered through the State Programme 'Digital Belarus' 2026-2030, which plans a national computing base for AI, AI systems for handling citizens' appeals and for security agencies, and a target of 15% of organisations using AI; presidential decrees that make AI the first priority for science and innovation in 2026-2030; and the 2017 digital economy decree, which gives AI developers, including those creating and training neural networks, High-Tech Park preferences. The 2021 personal data protection law provides the data protection baseline. An AI development concept, an AI law and an amendment on automated decisions are in preparation.
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 and 13 October 2026 from the National Legal Internet Portal; a run cut off by a usage limit was resumed and every record from it was re-checked against its official text. Not yet verified from the official text: any AI guidance from the data protection centre. The planned AI concept, AI law and data protection amendment are tracked as leads.

instruments.official_title: О Государственной программе «Цифровая Беларусь» на 2026–2030 годы (постановление Совета Министров Республики Беларусь от 30 декабря 2025 г. № 793)
instruments.english_title: On the State Programme "Digital Belarus" for 2026-2030 (Resolution of the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Belarus No. 793 of 30 December 2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: Council of Ministers of the Republic of Belarus (responsible customer: Ministry of Communications and Informatization)
instruments.current_status: Officially published on the National Legal Internet Portal on 10 January 2026 (No. 6-1/55630). Clause 3 of the resolution states it enters into force on 1 January 2026. It succeeds the State Programme "Digital Development of Belarus" 2021-2025 (Resolution No. 66 of 2 February 2021), which contains no AI provisions and is therefore not recorded. Current national digital programme; no separate national AI strategy or concept has been adopted (an AI development concept is in preparation, see leads).
instruments.summary: The Council of Ministers approves the national digital programme for 2026-2030, with the Ministry of Communications and Informatization as responsible customer and subprogrammes "Data Economy", "Digital State" and "Digital Sovereignty". Its AI section commits to a national platform for managing the life cycle of AI models (domestic software for running large language models without foreign servers), a system for collecting, anonymising and managing data for training AI models, a national corpus of datasets and language technologies for LLMs, and tools to adapt LLMs to sectoral and state tasks, including libraries of standard agents. It also lists AI measures for the state, including an AI-based national system for handling appeals from citizens and legal entities, a national computing base for AI, an AI resource-forecasting system for the Ministry of Defence and AI information-processing systems for the KGB, and tracks the share of organisations using AI as a programme indicator (target 15% by 2030).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main government programme steering AI development and public-sector AI use in Belarus.

instruments.official_title: Закон Республики Беларусь от 7 мая 2021 г. № 99-З «О защите персональных данных»
instruments.english_title: Law of the Republic of Belarus No. 99-Z of 7 May 2021 "On Personal Data Protection"
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of the Republic of Belarus (House of Representatives and Council of the Republic); signed by the President
instruments.current_status: Officially published on the National Legal Internet Portal on 14 May 2021 (No. 2/2819). Under art. 21, articles 1-19 enter into force six months after official publication (computed: 15 November 2021) and the other provisions on publication. In May 2026 the National Personal Data Protection Centre said a bill adding an article on automated processing and automated decision-making (including AI) is planned for submission to the Government (see leads). Text checked is the original published version.
instruments.summary: Belarus's general data protection law, adopted by the House of Representatives on 2 April 2021 and approved by the Council of the Republic on 21 April 2021. It sets legal bases for processing (consent and listed exceptions), rules for special and biometric data, data-subject rights and operator duties, and applies to processing with or without means of automation, so it governs personal-data processing in AI training and use. It does not yet contain a specific rule on automated decision-making.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main binding law governing personal data used by AI systems; the data protection authority has stated its requirements apply to processing with AI technologies.

instruments.official_title: Декрет Президента Республики Беларусь от 21 декабря 2017 г. № 8 «О развитии цифровой экономики»
instruments.english_title: Decree of the President of the Republic of Belarus No. 8 of 21 December 2017 "On the Development of the Digital Economy"
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Belarus
instruments.current_status: Officially published on the National Legal Internet Portal on 27 December 2017 (No. 1/17415). Under clause 16, clauses 13, 14 and 17 entered into force on publication and the other provisions three months after official publication (computed: 28 March 2018). Clause 1 extends the High-Tech Park special legal regime to 1 January 2049. Text checked is the original published version; later amendments to the decree and the High-Tech Park Regulations were not checked.
instruments.summary: Presidential decree on the digital economy that extends the High-Tech Park special legal regime (tax and legal preferences) to 1 January 2049 and opens it expressly to activities in the field of artificial intelligence and self-driving vehicle systems. The High-Tech Park Regulations it sets out list the creation and training of neural networks and other algorithms in specialised areas of AI as a permitted resident activity, and allow residents to prepare and systematise training datasets for neural networks. It also creates the legal framework for tokens and blockchain and lists AI among sixth-technological-order technologies.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding act that defines AI development and neural-network training as privileged activities under the High-Tech Park legal regime, the main legal framework for Belarus's AI industry.

coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-13, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. Resumed run: 4 earlier records re-checked 2026-10-13 (Digital Belarus summary corrected; others unchanged); Decree No. 8 of 2017 added. cpd.by 503 (curl and WebFetch); pravo.by search JS-only (etalonline.by and web search used); house.gov.by not searched directly. Decree 8 effective 2018-03-28 computed from clause 16 (three months after publication 2017-12-27); Law 99-Z effective 2021-11-15 computed from art. 21 (six months after publication 2021-05-14). Decree 8 kept: it names AI activities (creating and training neural networks, training datasets) as privileged High-Tech Park activities. Decree 135 binding_regulation under strategy. Later amendments to Law 99-Z and Decree 8 not checked. Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: pravo.by official publication (document cards + PDFs) and etalonline.by full-text search (not phrase-capable): no AI-specific law, deepfake offence or public-sector algorithm rule found; Law 99-Z on personal data and Decree No. 8 on the digital economy (High-Tech Park AI activities) recorded; AI amendments to it and an AI law are only planned (leads). Bills bank: nothing found.; Government: Council of Ministers and Presidential acts: Digital Belarus 2026-2030 programme, innovation programme 2026-2030 and science priorities decree recorded; 2021-2025 digital programme read (no AI content); digital-sovereignty concept read (passing AI mention, lead); AI concept and digital strategy 2026-2035 in preparation (leads). Ministry of Communications site searched.; Ministries: Education, Health (medical device registration resolution No. 211/2026 read: no AI provisions), Justice, Defence, Finance/Tax, Labour, Interior: searched, nothing AI-specific found.; Regulators: National Personal Data Protection Centre (site returned 503; no AI guidance found; planned bill as lead), National Bank (no AI rules found; 2023-2025 concept as lead), Gosstandart (no adopted AI standard found; lead), Operational and Analytical Centre, High-Tech Park: searched, nothing AI-specific found.. Not reached: cpd.by (HTTP 503 on 2026-10-12 and again on 2026-10-13 via curl and WebFetch); pravo.by internal legal-act search (JS form; used etalonline.by word search and web search instead); house.gov.by not searched directly.
